clue.text: Pamper those preferring " down under " for retirement?

definitions.meaning: to pamper is to cosset or spoil someone with too much comfort

definitions.text: those preferring " down under " for retirement?
definitions.meaning: people who like to retire for the night lying on goose down sleep on a mattress stuffed with plumes

explanation.surface: Indulge the folk who like to retire to Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down under' suggests Australia, but here it is the soft down you lie on, and 'retirement' is going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to cosset excessively; as a noun it is a mattress filled with plumage, the choice of anyone wanting soft down beneath them at night.

clue.text: Taking ages over return may remove one's character

parts.note: ages are long periods of time, eras

indicators.note: return means the word for 'over' is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning, as 'over' can

explanation.surface: Ageing as one comes back might rob a person of their personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' looks like personality but means a written letter, which a rubber can wipe out; 'return' turns RE into ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber is the tool that rubs out a written letter or symbol.

clue.text: The last place to have connexion with current affairs

definitions.meaning: the end of a line, such as a station where trains or buses finish their route
a point where a wire is fixed to carry electric current, current being the flow of electricity

explanation.surface: A final spot for keeping in touch with the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current affairs' reads as news, but it is electricity: a battery's connection post.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the idea of an end: a rail or bus route's final stop, and an electrical contact point on a battery or circuit.

clue.text: A castellan always at home .

parts.note: a castellan is the keeper of a castle; the proverb says a man of this nation's home is his castle, so at home he always keeps one

explanation.surface: A castle keeper who never goes out.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue rests on the proverb 'an Englishman's home is his castle': any such man in his own house is lord of a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb makes every man of that nationality the keeper of a castle whenever he is in his own house.

clue.text: James writing the Book of Samuel ?

definitions.text: James writing the Book of Samuel

parts.words: James writing the Book of Samuel
parts.note: not the Bible book: a Scottish writer named James wrote the famous life of Samuel Johnson

explanation.surface: A man called James is the author of a book of the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Book of Samuel' suggests the Bible, but the Samuel is Dr Johnson, whose Life was written by James Boswell in 1791.
explanation.definitionFit: James Boswell wrote the celebrated biography of Samuel Johnson, so he is the James who wrote Samuel's book.

clue.text: Botheration Where is the doctor?

parts.note: Dr is the usual abbreviation for doctor
the question 'where is he?' is answered 'he is at ...', so at stands for where

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry when the doctor cannot be found.
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as the answer to itself: the doctor is DR AT some place.
explanation.definitionFit: Drat is a mild exclamation of annoyance, like 'bother'.

clue.text: Affected by rust with carbon monoxide, black usher appears in red

parts.note: CO is the chemical formula of carbon monoxide

indicators.note: appears in means the usher's word goes inside the word for red

parts.note: taken as written
Black Rod is the official usher of the House of Lords, so the black usher is Rod

explanation.surface: A rusty item, and a Parliamentary official dressed in black showing up in red.
explanation.walkthrough: Black Rod is the usher of Britain's House of Lords; the clue gives 'black' as half his title, leaving ROD, which 'appears in' RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Metal that rust has eaten away is described as eaten or worn by corrosion.

clue.text: Outspoken direction after the third turning, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are judged by how they sound when spoken

parts.note: an instruction to take the next turning past the third and then go right: fourth right

explanation.surface: A blunt set of road directions given to a driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fourth right' is the direction to take after passing the third turning; said aloud it gives the word for blunt and candid.
explanation.definitionFit: A forthright person speaks frankly and directly, without holding back.

clue.text: Sinbad's bird has nothing to take care of-that's the style

parts.note: the roc is the giant bird of the Sinbad tales in the Arabian Nights
O is the shape of zero, nothing
c/o, CO, is the abbreviation for care of on a letter

explanation.surface: A legendary bird with nothing to look after: a fine way to live.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is an ornate decorative and architectural manner of the eighteenth century.

clue.text: They're put up by gunners in river-craft

indicators.note: in means the gunners' abbreviation sits inside the word for river boats

parts.note: barges are flat-bottomed boats used on rivers
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British Army

explanation.surface: Gunners on river boats firing salvoes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gunners' means the Royal Artillery; 'by' only links. The definition works both ways: gunners put up a curtain of fire, and engineers put up dams on rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery fire laid down as a curtain is said to be put up, and dams built across rivers are erected too.

clue.text: Stop messing about? Not this boat enthusiast

definitions.text: Stop messing about? Not this boat enthusiast

parts.words: Stop messing about? Not this boat enthusiast
parts.note: a creature from a children's novel who says there is nothing half so worth doing as messing about in boats

explanation.surface: Telling someone to stop fooling around, though not a lover of boats.
explanation.walkthrough: In Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows, Ratty the river creature declares nothing is half so worth doing as 'simply messing about in boats', so he would never stop.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratty, the boating-mad vole of The Wind in the Willows, is called by this name in the book.

clue.text: Press for curtain material

definitions.meaning: to press clothes is to smooth them with a hot flat appliance
the Cold War border dividing Europe was called a curtain made of this metal

explanation.surface: Ironing the fabric for some drapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Curtain material' looks like fabric, but it is the metal of Churchill's Iron Curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to smooth clothes; as a metal it named Churchill's Cold War curtain.

clue.text: Conjuring, a fashionable career

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in the in thing
a vocation is a calling or career

explanation.surface: Magic tricks as a stylish profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conjuring' suggests stage magic but here is the calling up of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Conjuring in its old sense is summoning spirits by spoken appeal, which is what an invocation does.

clue.text: Fiery 'creature alarms Dean Twist

indicators.note: twist means the letters of the preceding words are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: A fire-breathing beast frightens a cathedral dean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' rearranges ALARMS and DEAN together; 'Dean' and 'Twist' look like names but are fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend held that this lizard-like amphibian could live in fire, so it became a fire spirit.

clue.text: Made claim that is upheld

definitions.meaning: to have asserted something as true
kept in good repair or kept going

explanation.surface: A claim was put forward and backed up.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both asserted firmly and kept in working order or preserved.

clue.text: An old tip I am backing, chez Tusitala

parts.note: a vail was an old word for a tip or gratuity given to servants

indicators.note: backing means the word am is turned round and read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone backs an old racing tip at a Samoan home.
explanation.walkthrough: Tusitala, 'teller of tales', was the Samoans' name for Robert Louis Stevenson; his Samoan house was Vailima. 'Backing' turns AM into MA.
explanation.definitionFit: This was Robert Louis Stevenson's estate in Samoa, where locals called him Tusitala, so it is his home.

clue.text: What disgrace no motorway in one grand Empire State!

indicators.note: in means the 'no motorway' letters sit inside those from the rest of the clue

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
NY is New York, nicknamed the Empire State
taken as written
Britain's first motorway is the M1, written with letters as MI

explanation.surface: A protest that a great American state has no motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's first major motorway is the M1, and the clue reads its figure 1 as the letter I. 'In' puts the 'no motorway' letters inside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignominy is public shame or dishonour.

clue.text: And 12 ac is used to hunt the 13?

definitions.meaning: and plus the answer to 12 across reads as andiron, a metal support for logs in a hearth
a hound to chase the fiery creature of 13 across would be a hound for the flames

explanation.surface: A clue built on its neighbours: something used for hunting the creature at 13.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And' plus IRON (12 across) gives andiron, a log support in a fireplace; a hound that hunted salamanders would live in the flames.
explanation.definitionFit: It is another name for an andiron, the metal stand holding logs in a hearth, and fits a hound chasing a creature living in flames.

clue.text: Rum poem — rum. About one shop

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters are placed around the letter for one
rum means odd or strange, so the following letters are made strange by rearrangement

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: An odd poem about rum, and one shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'Rum' (meaning strange) signals the anagram of POEM and RUM; that mix goes 'About' I.
explanation.definitionFit: An emporium is a large store or trading place.

clue.text: Bee wine is inside this long-leggety creature

indicators.note: is inside means the wine sits within the letters of the word bee

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Bee wine is found inside this spindly insect.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the old Scottish prayer against 'ghoulies and ghosties and long-leggety beasties'; beastie is Scots for a small creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Beastie is the Scots word for a small creature, the one in the prayer's 'long-leggety' line.

clue.text: Troops' accommodation is unable to take in heavyweight men

indicators.note: to take in means the word for unable surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: can't means unable to
a ton is a very heavy weight
taken as written

explanation.surface: Soldiers' quarters are too small for heavy men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unable' gives the contraction can't, written without its apostrophe; it 'takes in' the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantonment is a military camp or quarters, especially in British India.

clue.text: Non-fit linesman

definitions.meaning: from the Latin tag 'poeta nascitur, non fit': such a person is born, not made
someone who writes lines of verse

explanation.surface: A football official who is out of condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Non-fit' looks like unfit, but it is Latin 'non fit', 'is not made'. A linesman here writes lines, not a football official.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin proverb says a versifier is born, not made, and a writer of lines of verse is such a person.

clue.text: Lusty youngster will one day stoop to conquer

definitions.text: Lusty youngster will one day stoop to conquer

parts.words: Lusty youngster will one day stoop to conquer
parts.note: a strong young bird of prey that, when grown, will swoop down on its prey, stoop being the falconer's word for that dive

explanation.surface: A vigorous young person will someday humble themselves to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoop to Conquer' recalls Goldsmith's comedy, but stoop is the dive of a bird of prey onto its quarry.
explanation.definitionFit: A young eagle grows into a hunter that dives, or stoops, onto its prey.

clue.text: Brave new world appeared in one of these storms

definitions.text: Brave new world appeared in one of these
definitions.meaning: Miranda's 'O brave new world' line comes from a Shakespeare play named after a storm

explanation.surface: A dystopian novel came out during a gale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brave New World' suggests Huxley's novel, but the phrase is Miranda's line in Shakespeare's The Tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means violent storms, and its singular titles the Shakespeare play containing 'O brave new world'.

clue.text: The whole piano may need topping up with oil

definitions.text: may need topping up with oil

parts.note: the sum is the whole amount
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A whole piano might need oiling.
explanation.definitionFit: A sump is the reservoir at the bottom of an engine holding its lubricating oil.

clue.text: Madly bleating, if sensible to feeling

indicators.note: madly means the letters of bleating are thrown into wild disorder

explanation.surface: A sheep bleats wildly if it is perceptive enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sensible' here means perceptible, not wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangible means able to be perceived by touch.

clue.text: Of all duchies this was Trollope's

definitions.meaning: the Latin genitive plural meaning of everything, of all
in Anthony Trollope's Palliser novels the great nobleman is the Duke of this name

explanation.surface: Trollope had the best of all dukedoms.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin means 'of all'; Trollope's Duke of Omnium was the richest peer in his Palliser novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'of everything', it was also the title of Trollope's fictional dukedom.

clue.text: Quietly peruse a tiny contribution describing Pooh-Bah's ancestry

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical abbreviation for quietly
to peruse is to read
the widow's mite in the Gospels is the classic tiny contribution

explanation.surface: Read a small offering softly, about a pompous official's family line.
explanation.walkthrough: In Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado, the haughty Pooh-Bah boasts of 'pre-Adamite ancestral descent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooh-Bah claims his family line goes back to before Adam, the first man.
